title: Active and passive voice
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T17:07:10Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches active and passive voice as grammar: they all cover narrative or speaker voice as personality built from diction, rhythm, attitude or form, so the new syntax point needs a new card.

draft.title: Active and passive voice
card: The doer of the action comes first and is clear. "The coach cancelled the match."
The action comes first and the receiver of the action is the subject. "The match was cancelled." The passive often uses a form of "be" plus a past participle.
The passive can leave out who did the action, as in "Mistakes were made." It can also add "by" to name the doer: "The match was cancelled by the coach."
Effect: the active feels direct and names who is responsible. A writer may choose the passive to put the focus on the action or the receiver, or to leave the doer unnamed.
draft.remember: Active names the doer up front. Passive can leave the doer out.

a.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
opts: The window was broken during the storm
The storm broke the window last night
A branch smashed the window in the storm
Strong winds shattered the window
a.why: In the right answer the window receives the action and the sentence does not say who or what broke it. The other three name the doer first, so they are active.
a.clue: Look for a sentence where the doer is missing.

b.q: A council spokesperson wants a notice that does not name who closed the pool. Which sentence does this?
opts: The pool has been closed until further notice
The council has closed the pool until further notice
We have closed the pool until further notice
Council staff closed the pool until further notice
b.why: The passive "has been closed" puts the action first and names no doer, so it suits the spokesperson. The other options are active and each names who closed the pool, even though some are shorter.
b.clue: Which sentence never says who did it?

a.best: The window was broken during the storm

b.best: The pool has been closed until further notice

problems.detail: The card says that in the passive "the action comes first", but its own example "The match was cancelled" puts the receiver (the match) first as subject. The passive moves the receiver to the front, not the action. This can confuse students about word order.
Why (b) repeats that the passive "puts the action first", when in "The pool has been closed" the receiver (the pool) comes first.

The clue "Look for a sentence where the doer is missing" suggests a passive is identified by the missing doer. The card says a passive can also name the doer with "by", so this hint teaches a shortcut that fails for passives like "The match was cancelled by the coach."

check.summary: Both answers are clear and correct. The card and why (b) say the passive puts "the action" first when it is really the receiver that comes first, and the clue for (a) implies a passive always lacks a doer.
